records.question: Relate the method rationale to Table 2: why use product/difference interactions, and which Harm-P variant obtains the best F1 and AUROC?
records.answer:
The difference's contribution seems minimal but can offer a 2% AUROC increase on some datasets, with real gains appearing when combined with the product.
The difference only improves some scenarios while the product improves most, and the full extent of the difference contribution appears when all features are considered.
On Harm-P, the Full architecture achieves the best F1 (80.01%) and AUROC (91.31%) among the variants.
On Harm-P, Concat + Product reaches F1 78.25% and AUROC 90.20%, below the Full architecture.

metadata.caption: Table 2: Ablation results on datasets FBHM, Harm-C, Harm-P, MultiOFF and Propaganda.
metadata.nearby_text: F1-score results are varied, but the full SimCLIP architecture tops the ablations on 2 out of 5 datasets, achieving near top score (within 1%) in two others. Accuracy is topped in 3 out of 5 datasets and AUROC on 4 out of 5. Overall the full architecture is the best performing one with some special cases; for example there are trade-offs in Harm-C and Harm-P; Accuracy and F1-Score are traded while AUROC remains high. The contribution of the difference seems minimal but in some datasets, it offers a 2% increase in AUROC, although the real gains of the difference come when combined with the product. Finally, the Propaganda dataset is small and multi-label, and increasing F1-score decreases accuracy and vice-versa while AUROC is within 50% which is close to random, meaning our model fails on this particular task. In FBHM, SimCLIP falls behind by 3% compared to the top performing method noting, however, that top models in this dataset are very hard to beat due to extensive use of ensembling beyond CLIP and other pre-processing techniques, including heavy optimization for the challenge. Some novel techniques like MOMENTA, used in other datasets, are outperformed by our model. The Harm-C and Harm-P models are similar in nature but different in their contents and semantics.
